title: The £180 Mistake

pre.en: What happened to the new trainers in June?
pre.zh: 新运动鞋六月出了什么事？
options: They got too dirty to clean.
Chen left them on the bus.

intro: 小陈一时冲动，花 180 英镑买了一双白色皮运动鞋，接下来的事情和他想的不太一样。读的时候留意比较级：much more expensive、a bit softer、a lot more stylish——比较级前面加 much、a lot、a bit，就能说出「贵得多」「软一点」。结尾也是一组比较。

sentences.en: So, back in March, I decided to treat myself.
sentences.zh: 三月那会儿，我决定犒劳一下自己。

sentences.en: It'd been a long week at work, and a walk down Oxford Street is my way of winding down.
sentences.zh: 上了一周累人的班，去牛津街走一走，是我放松的法子。

sentences.en: In a shop near Bond Street, I tried on a pair of white leather trainers.
sentences.zh: 在邦德街附近的一家店里，我试穿了一双白色皮运动鞋。

sentences.en: They were much more expensive than my old £35 pair.
sentences.zh: 它们比我那双 35 英镑的旧鞋贵得多。

sentences.en: But they were a bit softer, and a lot more stylish.
sentences.zh: 不过穿着软一点，样子也时髦多了。

sentences.en: "They're made by hand in Portugal," the assistant said.
sentences.zh: 「这是葡萄牙手工做的，」店员说。

sentences.en: "Trust me, they're worth the money."
sentences.zh: 「相信我，这钱花得值。」

sentences.en: So I splashed out £180 on them, which is more than I usually spend on shoes in a year.
sentences.zh: 于是我一咬牙花了 180 英镑，比我平时一整年买鞋的钱还多。

sentences.en: Tom wasn't impressed.
sentences.zh: Tom 可一点都不买账。

sentences.en: "Chen, that's a rip-off," he said.
sentences.zh: 「小陈，你这是被宰了，」他说。

sentences.en: "Shoes shouldn't cost more than a weekend in Paris."
sentences.zh: 「一双鞋不该比去巴黎玩个周末还贵。」

sentences.en: For three months, I wore them almost every day.
sentences.zh: 接下来三个月，我几乎天天穿着。

sentences.en: I kept cleaning them with a special brush.
sentences.zh: 我隔三岔五就拿专用刷子刷一遍。

sentences.en: And I never left them lying around in the hall like my other shoes.
sentences.zh: 也从来不像别的鞋那样，随手扔在门厅里。

sentences.en: In April, Tom tried to throw my old pair away, but I hid them in my wardrobe.
sentences.zh: 四月份 Tom 想把我的旧鞋扔了，我把它们藏进了衣柜。

sentences.en: Then, by June, the left sole was starting to come away.
sentences.zh: 结果到了六月，左脚鞋底开始开胶了。

sentences.en: One rainy morning, I was killing time at the bus stop when I felt cold water in my sock.
sentences.zh: 一个下雨的早上，我在公交站干等着，忽然觉得袜子里进了冷水。

sentences.en: The number 73 finally turned up, and as I stepped on board, the sole split in two.
sentences.zh: 73 路总算来了，我一脚迈上车，鞋底裂成了两半。

sentences.en: I sat there for forty minutes with one wet foot.
sentences.zh: 我就这么湿着一只脚坐了四十分钟。

sentences.en: On Saturday, I took them back to the shop.
sentences.zh: 周六我把鞋拿回了店里。

sentences.en: The manager turned them over slowly and pointed at the sole.
sentences.zh: 店长慢慢把鞋翻过来，指了指鞋底。

sentences.en: "I'm afraid that's normal wear and tear," she said.
sentences.zh: 「恐怕这属于正常磨损，」她说。

sentences.en: "White trainers tend to need a bit more care than other shoes."
sentences.zh: 「白色运动鞋本来就比别的鞋更需要保养。」

sentences.en: "After three months?" I said.
sentences.zh: 「才穿三个月？」我说。

sentences.en: She told me to email customer service if anything else came up.
sentences.zh: 她让我以后再有什么问题，就给客服发邮件。

sentences.en: Honestly, arguing with her felt like a waste of time.
sentences.zh: 说真的，再跟她争下去也是白费工夫。

sentences.en: So I walked home in my old £35 pair.
sentences.zh: 于是我穿着那双 35 英镑的旧鞋走回了家。

sentences.en: They're much uglier — and a lot drier.
sentences.zh: 丑是丑多了——可好歹不漏水。

cards.zh: 犒劳自己；给自己买点好的
cards.note: to buy or do something special for yourself that you enjoy
cards.tip: yourself 要跟着主语变：I treat myself、she treats herself；犒劳的东西用 to：treat yourself to a new bag。
cards.example: I finished the project early, so I treated myself to a long lunch.

cards.note: to relax after a busy or exciting time, especially before sleep
cards.tip: wind 在这里读 /waɪnd/，过去式是 wound /waʊnd/；不读「风」的 /wɪnd/。
cards.example: I usually wind down with a podcast after work.

cards.note: to put on clothes or shoes to see if they fit or look good
cards.tip: 宾语是名词时可放中间也可放后面：try the jacket on / try on the jacket；是代词时只能放中间：try it on。
cards.example: Can I try this jacket on, please?

cards.note: 当定语直接放在名词前：a leather bag、leather shoes。
比较级用 more stylish，不说 stylisher。
to be good enough to justify the price you pay
cards.tip: worth 后面直接接名词，不加 of：worth the money，不说 worth of the money；也常说 worth every penny。
cards.example: The course wasn't cheap, but it was worth the money.

cards.note: to spend a lot of money on something, usually something you do not really need
cards.tip: 花多少钱可以放在中间：splash out £500 on a sofa；介词用 on，不用 for。
cards.example: We splashed out on a nice hotel for our anniversary.

cards.note: not impressed 常用来委婉地说「不以为然」。
something that costs much more than it should
也能当动词：brush your teeth（刷牙）。
to leave things in places where they should not be, instead of putting them away
cards.tip: lying 是 lie（躺、放着）的 -ing 形式，不是「说谎」；英式也说 lying about。
cards.example: Please don't leave your keys lying around the office.

cards.note: 英式说法；美式常说 closet。
和 soul（灵魂）同音。
也说 come off：The handle came off.
to do something unimportant while you are waiting or have nothing to do
cards.tip: time 前面不加 the；说用什么打发时间可以接 by doing：kill time by reading the news。
cards.example: I killed time in a bookshop before the film started.

cards.note: to arrive, often late or when people are not sure you will come

cards.zh: 在车上；在船上；在飞机上
cards.note: on or onto a train, ship or plane
to return something you bought to the shop because it is wrong or broken
cards.tip: 代词放中间：take it back；它还有「收回（说过的话）」的意思：I take it back — you're right。
cards.example: If the charger doesn't work, just take it back.

cards.note: the damage that happens to something when it is used for a long time
cards.tip: 不可数名词，前面不加 a；常和 normal 连用。tear 在这里读 /teə/，和「眼泪」的 /tɪə/ 不同。
cards.example: The landlord can't keep your deposit for normal wear and tear.

cards.note: 前面一般不加冠词：call customer service。

cards.zh: 有什么事的话；万一出了状况
cards.note: if something happens that needs attention, especially something you did not plan for
something that is not useful or does not give good results
